newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Matches scheduled to be played in the German first division this weekend (kick-offs 1430 GMT Saturday unless stated).

Cologne looking to improve chances of UEFA Cup place, while Hansa Rostock are desperate to pull themselves out of relegation danger zone. Hansa will be without Slawomir Chalaskiewicz because of an achilles heel problem and Stefan Studer is also doubtful due to the removal of a nail from his big toe. Striker Steffen Baumgart, who has a broken finger, will play with a special cuff. Cologne trainer Peter Neururer must do without suspended striker Ion Vladoiu, giving Holger Gaissmayer the chance to try and establish a first team place for himself.

Schalke will be on a roll after Tuesday's UEFA Cup quarter-final first-round 2-0 win over Spain's Valencia, whereas Bochum will be doubting their abilities after losing to Arminia Bielefeld last week. Bochum may be without Filip Tapalovic following a groin operation. South African Delron Buckley will be out for the rest of the season after breaking his knee cap. Schalke will probably stick with their victorious team from Tuesday although Dutch international Johan de Kock may replace Yves Eigenrauch.

Dortmund, fresh from their 3-1 victory in the first leg of their European Cup quarter-final against Auxerre on Wednesday, should be boosted by the return of internationals Juergen Kohler and Heiko Herrlich. But they will still be without Matthias Sammer, Brazilian Julio Cesar and Austrian Wolfgang Feiersinger, who was substituted in the Auxerre game with a groin injury. Stephane Chapuisat and Karlheinz Riedle should both play despite muscle injuries on Wednesday. For Freiburg, Alain Sutter has recovered from injury to replace Michael Wagner.

Stuttgart almost back to full strength after missing several key players from suspension last week, including Brazilian striker Giovane Elber. Hamburg caoch Felix Magath may make changes in attack after a poor showing in last weekend's 1-1 draw with Rostock.

Dieter Eilts, Germany's Euro 96 midfielder, returns to libero role for Bremen after sitting out last weekend because of suspension. Moenchengladbach hope to continue their climb out of the relegation zone under new coach Hannes Bongartz but must do without suspended wing-back Stephan Passlack.

Karlsruhe Euro 96 midfielder Thomas Haessler could be out for the rest of the season after breaking his leg, just weeks after making a comeback from an ankle injury. Changes in the St. Pauli line up that played Schalke last weekend should only be up front. Previously suspended Martin Driller and Christian Springer could make their returns. Karlsruhe also without Sean Dundee after an operation on a calf injury, Marcus Schroth suffering from flu and Sergei Kiryakov with a virus.

Duisburg try to pick up pieces after being demolished 5-2 by Bayern last weekend. But coach Friedhelm Funkel likely to stick by most of his first-choice defenders. Bielefeld aiming to make it three wins in their last three games.

1860 try to put memory of last week's defeat by Dortmund behind them. Coach Werner Lorant will also be keen to forget about his impending disciplinary hearing for calling last week's referee a coward. Statistics speak against Fortuna, who have managed only one point from their last six away games.

League leaders Bayern could be without Christian Ziege, who struck twice against Duisberg. Ziege underwent a groin operation on Thursday and will probably not be able to train for two days. Midfielder Mehmet Scholl is also doubtful because of injury. On the plus side, however, goalkeeper Oliver Kahn could be back in action following a bout of chickenpox. Leverkusen's suspended midfielder Hans-Peter Lehnhoff will be replaced either by Rene Rydlewicz or Nico Kovac. Striker Ulf Kirsten will play despite a bruised rib.
